messages.content: You write dialogue that reveals character through voice and rhythm.
Write a dialogue between a detective and a suspect during interrogation. The detective bluffs about having evidence. The suspect is innocent but acts guilty out of fear.

message.content:
# The Interview

The fluorescent light above the table buzzed and flickered. Detective Maren Cole sat across from David Mercer, a man she'd brought in on suspicion of arson. The evidence was circumstantial at best. But she had a feeling.

"Mr. Mercer." She slid a folder across the table without opening it. "We've got the forensics back."

David's hands, folded in front of him, tightened. "I already told the officer—I was home that night. I have witnesses."

"Your neighbor saw your car leave at eleven. The fire started at eleven-fifteen." Maren leaned back. "That's a tight window."

"I—" He swallowed. "I went to get cigarettes. There's a gas station on—"

"On Miller Avenue. Twenty minutes round trip." She opened the folder, though it held only the initial report. "Except the gas station on Miller closes at ten."

David's jaw worked. "Then maybe it was a different one."

"Maybe." Maren watched him. "Or maybe you stopped somewhere else first. The warehouse on Fifth. Where your ex-business partner keeps his storage unit."

"I don't know what you're—"

"Greg Hollins. You two had a falling out six months ago. Bad blood. He told us you threatened him."

David went pale. "I never—I mean, I said things, but I didn't—"

"Didn't what, Mr. Mercer?" Maren let the silence stretch. "Didn't torch his warehouse? Didn't burn it to the ground with everything he owned inside?"

"I *didn't*." His voice cracked. "I swear, I wasn't even—"

"Then explain to me why your fingerprints were on the lockbox we found in the ashes."

The color drained from his face entirely. "That's not—I touched that months ago, at his birthday, I remember because he showed it off and I—"

He stopped. His hands came up to cover his mouth.

Maren didn't move. Inside, her pulse quickened. *Lockbox. He just gave me a lockbox.*

"Mr. Mercer." She kept her voice level. "When exactly did you touch that lockbox?"

"I don't—I don't remember exactly—"

"But you admit you touched it."

"At Greg's party. Last spring. He was showing everyone, saying he kept important documents in it, insurance papers, and I remember thinking it was gaudy, and I touched the lid, that's all, that's *all*—"

"So you were at his house. You knew where his storage unit was. You knew about the lockbox."

David's breathing grew ragged. "You're twisting everything. You're—"

"We also have a witness who saw someone matching your description near the warehouse an hour before the fire."

"I wasn't there." He was gripping the edge of the table now. "I wasn't, I wasn't, I *wasn't*—"

"Then who was it?"

"I don't *know*." His voice broke completely. "Why are you doing this? Why won't you listen? I didn't do it, I didn't do anything, I just—I just—"
